title: TermAl host aborts the process on a failed heap allocation under low system commit instead of degrading
outcome: When system commit is exhausted by another process, the TermAl host either survives (by refusing or deferring the work that needed the allocation) or exits in a recorded, recoverable way. It does not abort mid-operation with 0xc0000409 and lose every session's live state.
acceptance: The allocation site(s) that failed at 17:08:27Z on 2026-11-14 ("memory allocation of 2719744 bytes failed", termal.exe 0xc0000409, Application Error event) are identified from evidence: the event, any crash dump or journal, and the code paths that allocate about 2.7 MB buffers on hot paths.

Either the avoidable large allocation on that path is bounded or made fallible (e.g. try_reserve with a refusal reported to the caller), with a behavioural test that injects allocation failure or a size cap and observes the refusal instead of an abort; or the item records, with evidence, why Rust's global-allocator abort cannot be avoided there and what the host does instead (for example persisting state so a restart loses nothing).
